Primary care practice marketing

Primary Care Marketing Agency: Website Audits and Marketing for Family and Internal Medicine

Primary care marketing is mostly about access: which services you offer, whether you are accepting new patients, which insurance you take, how to book, and when. A practice that answers those questions clearly online fills appropriately; one that does not gets calls it cannot convert and loses patients it could have seen. We help primary care practices state their real capacity and services clearly.

In Houston, Dallas and Miami, primary care is already reserved for existing clients, so in those cities we offer a complimentary website audit and consultation rather than ongoing marketing.

Primary care is reserved in Houston, Dallas and Miami, and in many surrounding cities (including Katy, Sugar Land, Pearland, The Woodlands, Plano, Fort Worth, Hollywood FL and Fort Lauderdale). Practices there can request a complimentary audit and consultation only.

Where primary care marketing breaks

Marketing that promises more access than the practice has

The most common primary care problem we see is not invisibility; it is mismatch. Sites say ‘accepting new patients’ when panels are closed, list services offered by one provider as if all offer them, and hide hours and insurance information that patients need before calling.

Capacity not stated honestly

New-patient status, wait times and provider availability are missing or out of date.

Services listed, not explained

Chronic care, preventive visits and procedures appear as a list with no detail or provider link.

Office facts inconsistent

Hours, phone numbers and insurance differ between site, Google and directories.

Front desk overloaded

Patients call to ask questions the website could answer, tying up phone lines.

What we offer

Primary care website audit, and marketing where available

In reserved markets, including Houston, Dallas and Miami, the complimentary audit and consultation is the only service available. In open markets we can also implement and run ongoing work. We separate the two clearly below.

Audit: access information

Whether new-patient status, services, insurance, hours and booking are clear and consistent.

Audit: listings

Google profiles and directories for each office.

Audit: website health

Speed, mobile, errors, forms and portal links.

Audit: written priorities

Ranked findings and a video walk-through your team or vendor can act on.

Open markets only: implementation

Provider and service pages, office pages and listing fixes.

Open markets only: ongoing work

Local SEO, selected Google Ads, family practice and internal medicine practice marketing with reporting.

Read our article on marketing and SEO challenges for Texas primary care clinics. Urgent care and walk-in clinics are covered on our urgent care and ER SEO page.

Process

How the primary care audit works

In reserved markets the process stops after prioritization and hand-off.

  1. Request

    Send practice name, website, offices and ZIP codes.

  2. Assess

    We review public pages and listings; read-only analytics access is optional.

  3. Prioritize

    Findings ranked by impact on access clarity and phone load.

  4. Walk-through

    A video call with your administrator.

  5. Hand-off

    You keep the findings; in reserved markets we do not pitch ongoing service.

Illustrative finding format

How audit findings are written

Not a real client.

  • Issue: ‘Accepting new patients’ banner on all providers; two have closed panels.
  • Why it matters: creates calls the front desk must decline.
  • Fix: state status per provider; review monthly.
  • Owner: practice administrator and web team.

Availability

Primary care availability in Houston, Dallas and Miami

Primary care is our most heavily reserved specialty. Houston is our base; Dallas and Miami are served remotely.

Houston and most surrounding cities are reserved. Complimentary audit and consultation only.

Miami, Hollywood and Fort Lauderdale are reserved. Complimentary audit and consultation only.

Healthcare marketing in Miami

Primary care is also reserved in Austin, Round Rock, Orlando and Kissimmee. Practices in other cities can ask; an unlisted city is not automatically open. Where ongoing work is available, proposals are scope-based with fees, ad spend and one-time work separated, and cancellable with 7 days’ notice. See the Texas and Florida hubs.

Questions and audit request

Primary care marketing questions

For primary care owners and administrators.

Is primary care marketing available in Houston, Dallas or Miami?

No ongoing marketing is available there; primary care is reserved for existing clients in those cities and many surrounding ones. We offer a complimentary website audit and consultation instead.

What does a primary care marketing agency do?

Makes services, new-patient status, insurance, hours and booking clear online, keeps listings accurate, and, where appropriate, runs local SEO and ads, with reporting.

How should a practice present new-patient capacity?

Honestly, by provider if it varies, and updated regularly. Overstating capacity creates calls you cannot convert and frustrated patients.

What affects the cost where ongoing work is available?

Offices, providers, site condition and ads. Quoted after review.

What does the complimentary audit include?

Access information, listings, website health and a written priority list with a video walk-through.

How should we choose an agency?

Ask whether they represent a competitor nearby, how they report, who owns accounts and how you can cancel.

Request a primary care website audit

Complimentary. Ongoing primary care marketing is not available in Houston, Dallas or Miami.
